name: Bob
summary: Senior Project Manager delivering integration-heavy rollouts for logistics and health customers, known for taking red projects back to green without losing the customer. Seven years as a developer and tech lead before moving into project management, so designs and estimates get challenged. PMP, current.

competencies.keywords: Concurrent projects, go-live planning, cutover, hypercare, site readiness

competencies.name: Project Recovery
competencies.keywords: Red-to-green turnaround, root causes, re-baselining, go/no-go gates

experience.title: Senior Project Manager
experience.description: Warehouse and freight-forwarding software for logistics firms. Accountable to the Head of Delivery for three concurrent customer projects, and moved the delivery team from waterfall stage gates to two-week sprints inside quarterly gates.
bullets: Took over the customs filing module in Dec 2023, red and four months behind; phase one went live at all three customer sites on 18 Mar 2024 and the first live filing cleared that day.
On the customs module, moved two document types added with no change request into a signed phase-two change, fixed test data at 40 sample shipments and made the status call a weekly go/no-go.
Track and forecast budgets totalling $1.8M a year across the three projects; report variance and present all three at the monthly delivery review to the CEO, CFO and Head of Delivery.
Negotiate statements of work and rates with two offshore development vendors, including both annual renewals in 2024 and 2025, and approve vendor invoices before the PMO pays them.
Wrote the vendor scorecard (delivery against plan, defect escape rate, responsiveness) and use it in a quarterly performance review with each vendor.
Ran the RFP for the carrier API integration vendor: four bids scored with the head of engineering and the customer's IT lead; contract signed May 2023, first carrier live Sep 2023.
Paused the warehouse scanning rollout for two weeks after a bad first week on unsurveyed yard Wi-Fi, and added a site readiness checklist; all four warehouses live by Sep 2025.
Built the weekly status pack the PMO now uses for every project, from Jira exports via a Python tool published on GitHub; it replaced three formats.

experience.title: Project Manager
experience.description: Clinic scheduling and patient-records software for hospital groups. Moved from tech lead into project management to run the 14-month, $1.2M patient-records migration for a three-hospital group.
bullets: Found in dry run two that roughly 9 percent of about 410,000 records had conflicting identifiers; went live six weeks after the original date, on the re-baselined date agreed with the customer.
Ran the monthly steering committee with the hospital group's CIO and operations director; brought three costed options for the data-quality problem and got the new date agreed in writing.
Managed the data migration contractor whose first dry run took 31 hours against a 12-hour cutover window; their rewrite into parallel batches by hospital got dry run three under 9 hours.
Negotiated the HL7 interface supplier's shared specialist up from one to two days a week for the eight weeks before cutover, in return for our developers doing their own interface testing.
Ran the cutover command centre over the go-live weekend; when one hospital's ADT feed failed to reconnect, the supplier fixed it in about two hours and go-live went ahead on time on Monday.
Ran three months of hypercare, then the group's hosted upgrades (two major releases a year), an e-referrals interface and the move of its reporting database to the hosted environment.

experience.title: Tech Lead
experience.description: Promoted from senior developer to lead the clinic scheduling team (Java, Angular, PostgreSQL) after the previous tech lead left.
bullets: Led four developers and took releases from monthly to fortnightly in April 2017 by replacing the monthly release board with a checklist the team signed off; the cadence held.
Led the move of three hospital customers from on-premise to AWS; the first took eleven weeks against a six-week plan, so wrote a runbook and the next two took five and four weeks.

experience.title: Senior Software Developer
experience.description: Joined when each hospital integration was hand-coded and took a developer about six weeks. Built the HL7 v2 ADT interface adapter, driven by a per-hospital configuration file, that cut a typical integration to about two weeks and served 11 hospital integrations.

experience.title: Software Developer
experience.description: Card payment processor for small merchants. Developer on the Java/Spring settlement services, on call one week in four; rewrote the nightly reconciliation batch from an in-memory Java job to set-based SQL in PostgreSQL, cutting run time from about four hours to about 45 minutes.

credentialLines: Project Management Professional (PMP) - PMI - 2020, renewed 2023 and 2026 | Professional Scrum Master I (PSM I) - Scrum.org - 2019 | SAFe for Teams course (two days), 2024
Volunteer coding club mentor for teenagers, 2019 - present; wrote its twelve-week beginner Python curriculum in 2023.
